lines: There are seashells at the top of Mount Everest.
There are SEASHELLS at the TOP of Mount EVEREST.
[laughs] Seashells? Who hiked them up there, a very lost crab?
SEASHELLS? Who hiked them up there, a very LOST CRAB?
Nobody carried them. The summit used to be sea floor.
Nobody CARRIED them. The summit used to be SEA FLOOR.
[mischievously] Okay, I'm packing for Everest. Item one... a snorkel.
Okay, I'm PACKING for Everest. Item ONE... a SNORKEL.
Good plan. You're only about four hundred and fifty million years late.
Good plan. You're only about FOUR HUNDRED and FIFTY MILLION years LATE.
Back then, this rock was mud in a warm, shallow sea.
Back then, this ROCK was MUD in a WARM, SHALLOW SEA.
[curious] So who lived in my snorkelling spot?
So who LIVED in my SNORKELLING spot?
Trilobites, sea lilies, tiny shellfish. Their fossils are still up there.
TRILOBITES, SEA LILIES, tiny SHELLFISH. Their FOSSILS are still UP THERE.
[surprised] The highest rock on Earth... is an old aquarium?!
The HIGHEST rock on Earth... is an old AQUARIUM?!
Pretty much. Then India showed up.
Pretty much. Then INDIA showed up.
The plate! It drifted north and slammed into Asia, about fifty-five million years ago.
The PLATE! It drifted NORTH and SLAMMED into ASIA, about FIFTY-FIVE MILLION years ago.
That sea floor got squeezed, folded and shoved up... five and a half miles.
That SEA FLOOR got SQUEEZED, FOLDED and SHOVED up... FIVE and a HALF MILES.
[sarcastic] Item two: a tape measure. Because apparently it keeps changing.
Item TWO: a TAPE MEASURE. Because apparently it keeps CHANGING.
In 2020, Nepal and China remeasured it... almost three feet taller.
In 2020, NEPAL and CHINA remeasured it... almost THREE FEET taller.
Mostly better measuring. But it really is rising... about four inches a century.
Mostly better MEASURING. But it really IS rising... about FOUR INCHES a CENTURY.
[laughs] Four inches a century? My fingernails are faster.
FOUR INCHES a century? My FINGERNAILS are FASTER.
Lots. India's still pushing. So next time someone says they climbed Everest...
Lots. INDIA'S still PUSHING. So next time someone says they CLIMBED Everest...
[laughs] ...tell them they walked on the bottom of the sea.
...tell them they WALKED on the BOTTOM of the SEA.
